From: logistics_manager@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-02-22 11:00
Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

From: logistics_manager@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-02-22 11:00
Subject: Warehouse handling concern for item identifiers

Hi All,

During the warehouse pilot, the team raised a usability concern around how item identifiers are handled on labels and during scanning.

In daily operations, staff tend to refer to the machine-readable identifier as the barcode or serial code rather than by the formal term used in the specification. The current business-oriented format may be less convenient for the scanning workflow than a more scanner-friendly representation.

For now, please review whether the warehouse-facing identifier should remain just an operational alias in the UI, or whether a separate machine-readable identifier is needed alongside the formal item identifier. The main goal is to reduce ambiguity for staff and avoid slowing down intake and return handling.

Thanks,
Gary (Logistics)

resolvedConflictsOrObsolete: Current activity and audit views favor privacy-preserving identifier style that makes operational review harder for non-technical auditors, creating tension with human-readability requirement (E2)
resolutionNotes: R81b targets human-readable audit identity. PRIMARY evidence (E2, E3, E4) establishes that current privacy-preserving identifiers conflict with operational readability for non-technical auditors, and that a controlled identity-resolution path may be needed. E5 and E6 specify that audit logs must include user identifier and be available for administrative review. E3 and E7 raise the unresolved question of whether identities should be stored directly or resolved through a lookup layer. The core operative context centers on the requirement that audit identities be human-readable for authorized reviewers while maintaining privacy constraints. The critical gap is the unconfirmed audit model: direct vs. controlled-lookup identity resolution."
